node-1.label: A 7-year-old boy presented with behavioral issues since infancy.

node-2.label: Early developmental history: first child, unplanned pregnancy, oligohydramnios at 36 weeks, possible congenital cardiac defects noted in fetus; delivered preterm at 36 weeks via emergency cesarean section due to fetal bradycardia; birth weight 1.7 kg, delayed cry, and cyanosed at birth; cardiac evaluation at birth identified patent ductus arteriosus, ventricular septal defect, tricuspid regurgitation, and a left atrium to right atrium shunt, and he was started on digitoxin.

node-3.label: As he grew, he exhibited global developmental delay and was diagnosed with bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss at 6 months of age; over time he continued to show delayed milestones and developed poor eye contact, poor social and communication skills, repetitive head rocking, hand flapping movements, and a preference for fixed routines.

node-4.label: From the age of 3, he displayed symptoms of attention deficit hyperkinetic disorder (ADHD), including an inability to sit still for more than 2-3 minutes and difficulty engaging in activities; his insistence on routine and hyperactivity increased over the years, leading to aggressive behaviors such as hitting and biting his mother, which resulted in significant distress and a psychiatry consultation with subsequent admission to a child psychiatry inpatient unit; there was no history of head injury, seizures, frequent diarrhea and vomiting, birthmarks, or failure to thrive.

node-5.label: Physical examination revealed a small head circumference (49 cm) and bilateral flat feet; mental status examination showed a lack of eye contact, hyperactivity, irritable mood, frequent side-to-side head movements, and hand flapping; his intelligence quotient was evaluated to be 25.

attrs.why: The radiologist independently affirms the autism with profound intellectual disability phenotype and notes that the MRI and ophthalmologic findings reflect the underlying etiologic process rather than altering the behavioral diagnosis. Together with poor eye contact, repetitive head rocking, hand flapping, routine insistence, aggression, microcephaly and IQ 25, the phenotype remains best explained by autism with profound ID, so confidence is held at 0.85.

The radiologist explicitly endorses that the multifocal symmetric white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensities combined with pigmentary retinopathy suggest a genetic/metabolic syndrome, reinforcing the unifying picture that also includes congenital cardiac defects, preterm birth, global delay, hearing loss and microcephaly. This strengthens the genetic syndromic hypothesis, raising confidence slightly from 0.75 to 0.77, still limited by unavailable genetic/metabolic testing.

Congenital infection remains possible and cannot be excluded because TORCH testing is unavailable. The specific constellation of profound sensorineural hearing loss, pigmentary retinopathy and patent ductus arteriosus additionally raises a congenital rubella consideration, but the absence of failure to thrive and birthmarks keeps this less likely than a genetic cause, so confidence is held at 0.45.
node-4: ADHD symptoms, hyperactivity, aggression; but node-3 and node-5 show autism features and profound ID, making pure ADHD less likely.

node-12.label: Genetic/metabolic disorder with retinal and white matter involvement (possible leukodystrophy)
